Charcot's triad is specific but insensitive — do not wait for all three (or for Reynolds' pentad) before treating suspected
cholangitis; it is a biliary emergency.
Ascending cholangitis needs biliary decompression (usually ERCP), not antibiotics alone — drain the duct, urgently in Grade III
or if there is no response.

reserve the drain for the genuinely unfit.
Suspect Mirizzi with a stone in Hartmann's pouch and jaundice — the bile-duct-injury and gallbladder-cancer risks warrant a
low threshold for subtotal / open surgery.
